faq.q: How can a river cut through rock?
faq.a: Water alone is weak, but rivers carry sand, gravel and boulders that grind the riverbed like sandpaper, especially in floods. Over millions of years this cuts very deep.
asks: How was the Grand Canyon made?

faq.q: Why does uplift help make canyons?
faq.a: As plate forces slowly push the land up, the river gets steeper and faster, so it cuts down harder. The Colorado Plateau rose while the Colorado River cut down, making the Grand Canyon.
The walls show layers of different rock laid down at different times. Each has its own colour, and hard layers form cliffs while soft ones form slopes.
asks: Why does the Grand Canyon have layers?

faq.q: How old is the Grand Canyon?
faq.a: Most of the canyon was carved in the last 5 to 6 million years, but the rocks in its walls are far older, nearly 2 billion years at the bottom.
asks: When did the Grand Canyon form?

faq.q: Why are canyons common in dry places?
faq.a: In deserts there are few plants to soften slopes, and rare heavy rains cause flash floods that cut fast. The steep walls stay steep because there is little rain to wear them back.

facts: The Grand Canyon is about 446 kilometres long and up to about 1.8 kilometres deep.
Most of the Grand Canyon was carved by the Colorado River in the last 5 to 6 million years.

quiz.say: In a canyon wall, which rock layer is usually oldest?
quiz.why: Layers were laid down one on top of another, so the bottom ones are oldest.

wrong.1: The top layer was laid down last, so it is youngest.
wrong.2: Colour depends on the minerals, not age.
